description: The bar chart, titled “PHEME,” illustrates the accuracy (%) of a multimodal misinformation detection model across five ablation variants: “Ours” (the full model), “w/o comments,” “w/o text,” “w/o select,” “w/o emotion,” and “w/o cognition.” The vertical y-axis represents accuracy percentage, ranging from 75.0 to 92.5 in increments of 2.5, while the horizontal x-axis lists the model variants. Each bar is color-coded and labeled with its exact accuracy value: “Ours” (dark red, 89.84%), “w/o comments” (orange, 86.82%), “w/o text” (light yellow, 80.10%), “w/o select” (light blue, 88.80%), “w/o emotion” (medium blue, 87.34%), and “w/o cognition” (dark blue, 87.17%). The chart visually demonstrates that removing textual input (“w/o text”) causes the largest drop in performance, while the full model (“Ours”) achieves the highest accuracy. The bars are not sorted by value but appear in a fixed experimental order, with “Ours” on the far left and “w/o cognition” on the far right. The chart is presented at a slight tilt, and all bars are solid-colored with no error bars or additional annotations. The second, partially visible chart on the right appears to be labeled “PON” and shows similar ablation results with higher overall accuracy values (e.g., “Ours” at 90.57%), suggesting a comparison across datasets or tasks.
